frase_gancho.texto: A young warrior peers out from between the open jaws of an eagle.

puente_narrativo.texto: From the delicate art of obsidian, we move on to the military world: a stone head that speaks of the empire’s warrior orders.

guion_corto.texto: It is called the Eagle Warrior, but what you have before you is only a head, 32 centimeters high. It belongs to a young man of the high nobility, who peers out from between the open jaws of a helmet shaped like an eagle. His face is serene and firm. At the nape of his neck he wears a pleated paper bow, an ornament that almost no one notices. Eagle warriors formed, together with the jaguar warriors, the two highest military orders of the Mexica empire. They were associated with the sky, the sun, light and heat. It is believed that wearing the helmet meant taking on that identity: ceasing to be merely a man in order to become the bird of the Sun. It is a work sculpted in stone, from the Late Postclassic.

guion_largo.texto:
It is called the Eagle Warrior, but what you have before you is only a head. It measures 32 centimeters high and is sculpted in stone, in the Late Postclassic. It is small, but it has the strength of a complete figure.

The face of a young man, serene and firm, peers out from between the open jaws of a helmet shaped like an eagle’s head. The sculptor sought contrast: a calm, human face, framed by the beak and feathers of a bird of prey. There is a detail at the nape of the neck, a pleated paper bow, an ornament characteristic of these warriors.

Eagle warriors, called cuauhtli, were one of the two most prestigious military orders of the Mexica empire. The other was that of the jaguar warriors. Each order had its own world. The eagles were linked with the sky, the sun, light, heat and the masculine principle.

For the Mexica, the eagle was the bird of the Sun. That is why a warrior who wore its helmet was not merely dressing up. It is believed that, by putting it on, he took on the strength and the destiny of the eagle, which accompanies the Sun across the sky. The sculpture captures that idea: the young man does not cease to be human, but he wears the bird around his face.

It is a small piece, but it sums up how the Mexica joined war, the Sun and nobility in a single image.

texto: Look for the serene face peering out from between the eagle’s open jaws.
Find the pleated paper bow at the nape of the neck.
Notice the helmet shaped like an eagle’s head that surrounds the face.

texto.Dimensions: 32 cm high x 30 cm wide x 26 cm long

texto.pregunta: Myth: The Eagle Warrior is a full-body, life-size figure.
texto.respuesta: Reality: This piece is a head sculpted in stone, 32 centimeters high, which shows the face of a young man inside the eagle helmet.
